title: Introduce token-flow sentinels and saturation hysteresis for VPC upgrade automation
creator: Aria Chen
description: Add a new category of lightweight probes, called 'token-flow sentinels', to improve VPC private deployment upgrade safety and to provide early detection of token saturation and tail-latency regressions. Work spans Terraform/IaC module additions, probe operator changes, alerting rules, and a gated canary rollout for upgrades. The goal is to stop unsafe upgrades quickly and automatically when token throughput, queue depth, or user-facing latency deviate from expected baselines.
background: Current VPC upgrade runbooks rely on broad SLO dashboards and manual inspection of GPU metrics. We have seen two close-calls in the last year where a quantization kernel change caused token emission stalls under certain batch mixing patterns, leading to user-visible p99 spikes. Existing probes (synthetic and infra-level) are valuable but either too coarse or too slow to detect token-level flow issues during canaries. Token-flow sentinels will instrument request counts, per-connection KV CNT hits, enqueue durations, and a derived 'tokens_in_flight' gauge to create high-sensitivity gates for upgrade rollouts.
design_decisions: Probes live in the Terraform vpc_observability module as optional resources that can be turned on per-customer by feature flag.
Use a mix of push and pull metrics: agent exports tokens_in_flight and enqueue_ms; Prometheus rules evaluate short windows (30s, 5m) for fast gating.
Define hysteresis on saturation: two thresholds (warning and trip) with a 2-minute sustained window for trip to avoid flapping during short bursts.
Canary gating uses three metrics: p95 request token latency, 5xx error rate, and tokens_in_flight normalized to capacity; all must pass for next stage.
For private deployments where Prometheus scraping is disallowed, the VPC agent will expose a signed probe push endpoint that the Cloud Ops prometheus relay scrapes.
Keep default thresholds conservative to avoid customer noise; expose variables in Terraform for customers to tune to their capacity profiles.
implementation_notes: Terraform: add resource 'redwood_vpc_probe.token_flow_sentinel' with args: probe_type, threshold_warn, threshold_trip, window_sec, hysteresis_sec, alert_policy_id.
Kubernetes: update vpc-agent helm chart with export metrics 'tokens_in_flight', 'enqueue_ms', 'kv_cache_hit_rate', 'model_response_tokens_per_req'.
Prometheus: add recording rules for tokens_per_gpu = sum(tokens_in_flight)/sum(gpu_capacity) and alert rules for token_saturation_warning and token_saturation_trip.
Console: create per-customer dashboard 'vpc-token-sentinels' and a rollout gating widget that reads the three gating metrics together.
Security: signed push endpoint requires mTLS; Terraform module will create a signed cert secret when probes_enabled=true.
Add e2e tests in infra-ci that simulate token stalls by delaying the token emission path in a canary image and assert the upgrade is halted.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module accepts probes_enabled and creates probe resources without breaking existing installs.
Agent emits tokens_in_flight and enqueue_ms metrics with <100ms overhead in steady state.
Canary upgrade pipeline halts automatically at stage gates when token_saturation_trip fires in lab canary tests.
Onboarded demo customer (staging) shows no noisy alerts for a 48-hour steady workload with default thresholds.
Runbook with clear rollback steps and owner rotation is published and linked from the alert policy.
monitoring_queries: tokens_in_flight / gpu_capacity (5m avg) -> expected < 0.65 (warn at 0.75, trip at 0.9)
kv_cache_hit_rate (1m avg) -> warn if < 60% and trip if < 40% when tokens_in_flight > 0.8
rollout_plan: Stage 0: feature flag on, probes registered but alerts muted (observability-only) for 48h.
Stage 1: canary 5% of traffic for 30m. Gate: pass all three metrics for 30m window or abort and rollback to previous runtime image.
Stage 2: canary 25% for 60m. Gate: sustained pass for 60m and no escalations from on-call.
Stage 3: 100% rollout with monitoring at 1h and 24h checkpoints; auto-rollback if trip fires at any stage.
Emergency rollback criteria: token_saturation_trip OR p95 latency increase > 2x baseline AND 5xx rate > 1% sustained 5m.
